To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the normsbased approach to relational contracts, which is the most common in the literature, is not supported by empirical studies.
relational contract theory, as it stands, is not a theory.

(1) the normsbased approach to relational contract theory is not contradictory to the incomplete contracts approach; (2) empirical studies do not confirm the theoretical findings; (3) the empirical evidence does confirm that relational contracts are not necessarily based on formal legal contracts but may be based on a number of different types of contract; and (4) the umbrella agreements approach to relational contracts may provide an alternative theoretical basis to that of incomplete contracts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the theoretical approaches to relational contracts may be reconciled with empirical findings.
how firms can manage their contracts and relationships with their suppliers and customers.
the way in which contracts are constructed and the way that they are interpreted.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
relational contracts theory is a useful but not a complete explanation of the phenomenon of relational contracts and that further research is required.
relational contract theory is not yet a coherent and complete theory of contracts.

relational contracts are not a contradiction but a confirmation of the normative approach and that empirical research does not contradict the theoretical approaches but rather confirms the need for further research into the nature, form and content of relational contracts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

relational contract theory is a valuable lens through the which exchange relationships between companies or individuals can studied, but that the results of the empirical studies do not confirm the theoretical studies.
the theoretical studies are not contradictory and the empirical studies do not conform to those that would be expected as a direct result of the theoretical work.
relational contract theory, as a body of theory, is not contradictory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many ways of understanding and explaining the nature and form of relational contracts.
the theoretical approaches of relational contract theory and the results of empirical work do not always match.
, while the theoretical approaches to relational contracts have much to offer, the empirical evidence is often contradictory and that there is still a great deal of work to be done in the area.
